prompt: Which correctly reads a file and handles the potential IOException?
choices: try { FileReader fr = new FileReader("f.txt"); } catch (Exception e) {}
try (FileReader fr = new FileReader("f.txt")) { /* use fr */ } catch (IOException e) { e.printStackTrace(); }
explanation: try-with-resources closes fr automatically. Catching IOException (not bare Exception) is more specific and best practice. Option A doesn't compile (uncaught checked exception). Option B silently swallows the error. Option D is an invalid cast.
